evidence: Source-level design passes. Each time-varying, interactive or viewport promise in the public brief is graded by a judge step that acts or waits, never by a first paint. (1) Time-varying behaviour. hireops_rules.md section 5 (lines 120-128) promises updates within 15 s without reload: moves, new cards, unread counts, messages and seen marks. Each one has a timed criterion. Functional: hro_live_board (judge.toml ~line 301, protocol V), hro_msg_exchange (~310), hro_unread_counts (~346), hro_unread_scrolled_up (~355), hro_seen (~364). Polish: hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread. functional/prompt.md:59 and polish/prompt.md:18 make each such step one browser_run_code_unsafe action. In that action the trigger runs in an independent context, t0 is taken only after the trigger succeeds, and the DOM is polled every 500 ms up to 15000 ms with no click, type, scroll or reload of the watched page. The judge then waits 2000 ms more and reads counts, focus, scroll and draft. A negative leg is watched for the full 15 s and confirmed in a fresh context. Void attempts are defined and repeat at most twice, and a completed met=false is final. This satisfies Colderwater lessons 7 and 14. (2) Interaction. Every graded action is performed through clicks or keys: moves and refusals via ordinary non-drag controls; multi-select with a held modifier (app_context.md:33-35, lesson 8); Shift+Enter vs Enter and focus after send (hro_msg_compose); drafts across conversation switch, Board and reload (hro_drafts); bringing in earlier messages with a getBoundingClientRect anchor (hro_pol_earlier_place); keyboard focus after a refused move read via document.activeElement (hro_refused_put_back); a send aborted with route/setOffline, then retried (hro_pol_failed_send); a session ended in a second tab, then Enter pressed (hro_pol_session_resume); a real restart_app (protocol D). Preservation during live updates is read, not assumed. The open details, exact note text, activeElement, scroll offset and 'typing more appends' are checked in hro_pol_live_board, and draft, focus and stay-at-newest in hro_pol_live_thread. The 'appends' leg catches a caret reset. (3) Viewport and theme. instruction.md says 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout'. visual/prompt.md:14 says 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required.' The template's 390x844 and per-theme legs were removed in line with the brief, so no resize or theme toggle is owed, and a conforming app without them is not penalised. Drag is optional and never required. Both scored timed prompts carry 'Report every step' (lesson 9). Weak-app probes: (a) an app that updates only on focus or mouse movement fails, because the watched page must not be touched during polling; (b) an app that re-renders and re-inserts the note text fails on activeElement or on 'typing more appends'; (c) a 30 s poll fails the 15 s bound; (d) an app that marks seen when the Observer opens fails the 15 s negative watch in hro_seen. Conforming-alternative probes: SSE, socket and polling transports are all allowed. A board that scrolls in a container rather than the page is allowed. A CSS move animation is covered by the 2000 ms settle. No exact routes or selectors are assumed. Runtime evidence: the raw-evidence hashes match, and the scripted golden (results/workspace.json) passes the live board (arrival_ms 800, note draft and focus kept), the conversation arrival while scrolled up (draft, focus and scroll kept), and drafts, seen and unread updating live. That is a scripted Playwright run, not the configured claude-code/GLM judge, so no evidence exists that the judge actually performs these steps within budget.
risk_reasons: No full configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'). Whether the claude-code/GLM judge actually runs the 15 s polling actions, rather than scoring a still page, is unmeasured. browser_run_code_unsafe actions that combine an independent sign-in, the trigger, 15 s of polling and a 2 s settle have not been shown to fit the MCP tool's limits.

Polish workload is unmeasured: judge.toml timeout = 900 s covers the gate, adding up to 12 cards through the UI so the board scrolls, and five interactive rows that each sign in an independent context. If the budget runs out, the interactive rows become 'NOT EXERCISED' and score 0. Workload is measured, not inferred (REVIEW_POLICY), so this is an evidence gap, not a Fail.

The scripted golden does not exercise every interactive leg the judge is told to run. workspace.cjs:382-399 moves the opened card itself (Di Four), while hro_pol_live_board says 'moves a different card'. It never scrolls the board or checks its scroll offset. No golden leg aborts a send for hro_pol_failed_send (threads.js:195 and app.js:31 show source handling only). Golden behaviour for these interactive legs is therefore unmeasured.
notes: P3 (precision, not a defect). In protocol U's scrolled-up leg, 'stays unread until he goes to it' is read once, at the settled point after the notice appears, not watched for the full 15 s as a negative. An app that marks the message read a few seconds late while the user is still scrolled up could pass. Optional fix: say the unread count is watched until the end of the 15 s window before Rafael goes to the message.

P3. The brief's 'whether I am reading or halfway through a reply, never touch my draft or my cursor' is tested for draft and focus only at the newest message (hro_pol_live_thread). The draft is not tested while scrolled up. A fault that touches only that combination is implausible.

hro_refused_put_back does not say to wait for the server's refusal before reading the card's stage. An optimistic UI read mid-flight could show the card in Interview, but the leg 'the reason is shown' implies reading after the refusal. Local latency makes this negligible.
